title: JSON contract monitoring & calibration for low-bit function-call outputs
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Problem: When serving models quantized to FP8/INT8 we observe an uptick in structured-output failures specifically for function-call (fn_call) JSON payloads. Failures range from minor field drift (e.g., numeric fields rounded into strings) to out-of-schema objects that break downstream tooling. Current CI focuses on token-level perplexity and end-to-end quality; we do not have a lightweight continuous guardrail that flags JSON contract regressions per-quant-profile or recommends calibration adjustments.

Goal: Build a JSON contract monitoring and calibration pipeline that: 1) continuously measures schema adherence and semantic contract fidelity across quantization profiles (FP8/INT8 variants), 2) ties failures to calibration knobs (per-layer scale, activation clipping, histogram bucket ranges) and runtime kernels, and 3) produces actionable calibration suggestions and safe fallback policies for the runtime (e.g., auto-fallback to higher precision model variant or trigger post-process repair). The deliverable for this ticket is the first end-to-end iteration: an automated validation job, a small calibration suggestion engine, and CI gating rules for critical endpoints.

Scope & Non-goals:
- In-scope: synthetic and sampled production prompt corpus, schema conformance rate, per-field error types, simple repair heuristics, metrics dashboard and PR check integration.
- Out-of-scope: full retraining or fine-tuning to address quantization failure modes, full GUI in Console (we will surface metrics via internal dashboards and links).

Why now: Recent Dedicated customer reported regressions in structured billing outputs after enabling INT8 quantization for cost reasons. Quick detection + actionable calibration decreases customer churn and enables more aggressive cost tuning.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Schema-conformance rate >= 99.5% for baseline-hosted workload on FP8-lite profile within two calibration passes.
- Mean time to detection for new regression <= 1 hour after build promotion.
- Suggested calibration changes resolve > 60% of conformance failures automatically in the validation harness without requiring model re-export.
acceptance_criteria: A nightly job runs per-quant-profile that reports schema-conformance percentage and per-field error breakdown for the selected prompt corpus.

A proof-of-concept calibration suggester that maps observed error classes to a small set of actionable changes (e.g., increase activation clip for layer X by delta, bump per-tensor scale for embedding layer).
CI gate that blocks a quantized model promotion if schema-conformance drops below configured threshold for critical routes.
Dashboard link with historical trend and a way to view failing example prompts and model traces (KV cache token offsets, generated tokens).
test_plan: Collect 2k representative prompts (mix of production-sampled fn_call traces + synthetic edge prompts) and annotate expected JSON schemas.
Run quantized variants (FP8-lite, FP8-aggressive, INT8-default) through the validation harness producing schema parse results and token-level diffs.
Classify failures into categories: parse-error, type-mismatch, missing-field, extra-field, semantic-mismatch (value range), and malformed-utf8.
Apply calibration suggester to top-3 failure modes; re-run harness to measure improvement. Log delta in conformance and token-level recovery.
Ensure CI integration: open a test PR with a deliberately bad quant profile to validate the gate (should fail).
updates: 2026-02-25 - Ticket created by Marco Alvarez. Initial scoping and KPIs discussed with PM/DS. Assigned to Aisha.

2026-02-27 - PoC harness skeleton checked in: tools/quant-json-guard repo created. Contains runner that calls existing structured-output fuzzer and schema checker. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-json-guard/pull/1
2026-03-03 - Early results: FP8-aggressive shows 2.1% schema failures on sampled billing prompts; INT8-default shows 0.7%. Noted parse-errors concentrated in numeric fields and in nested arrays.

2026-03-05 - Spike: collected histogram profiles per-layer from INT8 export and compared to FP8; observed per-tensor scale mismatch in attention projection (proj_k) correlating with missing numeric keys. WIP doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QP/Histogram+spike+analysis

2026-03-08 - Calibration suggester v0 implemented (rule-based): maps failure categories to adjustments (activation clip + per-tensor scale delta + bias folding enable). Ran on 200 examples: resolved ~48% of failures for FP8-aggressive.

2026-03-10 - Design review with Runtime team: agreed fallback policy semantics — runtime will attempt schema-aware postprocess repair for non-critical fields, and if repair rate < 40% escalate to auto-fallback to FP16 variant for that route. Notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quant-profiles/meeting-notes
2026-03-12 - Added CI gate prototype to internal test harness. Blocking rule can be toggled per-route. Next: expand corpus and add token provenance traces to failing examples.
Blockers: need access to larger production prompt sample (privacy check pending) and a standardized mapping between model export kernel names and runtime layer identifiers.
Planned next: instrument per-token confidence scoring in harness and add calibrated fallback thresholds to runtime (owner: runtime-team).
